summary:
Orbit Health Atlas

Exploring the connection between human health and space exploration.

Orbit Health Atlas is an interactive educational platform designed to make NASA's human spaceflight research more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand.

The project brings together scientific information from NASA's Human Research Program, focusing on the five major hazards of human spaceflight, the risks astronauts face during space missions, and ongoing research aimed at protecting human health in space.

Through an intuitive interface, interactive 3D visualizations, and accessible scientific content, the platform helps users explore how the space environment affects the human body and why research is essential for the future of space exploration.

Orbit Health Atlas also aims to connect space science with knowledge that can inspire scientific curiosity, education, and a better understanding of human health on Earth.

Our mission is to transform complex space health research into an accessible and interactive learning experience for everyone.
details:
Orbit Health Atlas

1. Project Overview

Orbit Health Atlas is an interactive educational platform designed to explore the effects of spaceflight on human health. It transforms scientific information from NASA's Human Research Program (HRP) into an accessible visual experience, helping users understand the challenges astronauts face during space missions.

The platform combines scientific content, interactive 3D environments, simulated health indicators, and educational resources to connect human physiology with space exploration.

2. Main Features

Interactive Mission Dashboard

The main dashboard presents a simulated astronaut health monitoring environment, displaying indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, glucose levels, sleep duration, and emotional well-being.

Users can explore different simulated scenarios, including normal conditions, fatigue, and situations requiring attention. These simulations demonstrate how health indicators may change under different conditions.

The Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight

The platform explores the five major hazards identified by NASA's Human Research Program:

  • Space Radiation
  • Isolation and Confinement
  • Distance from Earth
  • Gravity Fields
  • Hostile and Closed Environments

Each hazard is presented through interactive visual elements and educational explanations.

Human Spaceflight Health Risks

Orbit Health Atlas organizes NASA's identified health risks into three major categories:

  • Physiological risks
  • Behavioral risks
  • Radiation-related risks

Users can explore individual risks, understand their relationship with spaceflight hazards, and access related NASA resources.

Ongoing NASA Research

A dedicated research section presents studies associated with NASA's Human Research Program, helping users discover ongoing scientific investigations and understand how research contributes to astronaut safety and mission preparation.

3D Visualization and Communication Simulation

The platform uses interactive 3D visualizations to represent spaceflight hazards, health risks, and scientific information.

It also includes a communication delay simulator that estimates signal travel time between Earth and different destinations, such as the International Space Station, the Moon, and Mars. This feature demonstrates how distance affects communication during space missions.

Interactive Support Assistant

A floating support assistant helps users navigate the platform, understand its sections, and find guidance on using the available information.

3. Scientific Foundation and Data Sources

The project uses publicly available scientific information and educational resources from NASA, particularly the Human Research Program.

Key references include:

  • NASA — Human Spaceflight Hazards
  • NASA — Risks of Human Spaceflight
  • NASA — Ongoing Human Research Program Studies
  • NASA — Human Research Roadmap

These resources provide the scientific foundation for the educational content presented throughout the platform.

4. Technology and Development

Orbit Health Atlas was developed as a web-based application with an interactive and responsive interface.

Its main technologies include:

  • React and TypeScript for the application structure.
  • Three.js-based components for interactive 3D visualizations.
  • Interactive charts and dynamic data displays.
  • Simulation logic for astronaut health indicators and communication delays.

5. Project Impact and Purpose

Space exploration requires a deeper understanding of how the human body responds to extreme environments. Radiation exposure, altered gravity, isolation, limited resources, and communication delays are important challenges for future missions.

Orbit Health Atlas aims to make these complex topics easier to explore and understand.

By combining scientific information with interactive technology, the project encourages scientific curiosity, supports space education, and helps people recognize the importance of human health research for the future of exploration beyond Earth.

Our vision is to bring space health science closer to everyone, turning complex research into knowledge that inspires discovery, learning, and innovation.

Note: Health indicators displayed in the dashboard are simulated for educational purposes. They do not represent real astronaut telemetry, clinical measurements, or medical diagnosis.
